method.command: PYTHONHASHSEED=0 PYTHONPATH=src py-spy record --format raw --rate 100 --gil --threads --full-filenames -- python3 -m twixt_ai.evaluation.cuda_selfplay_512_cli --output-dir /path/to/scratch/selfplay-out --report /path/to/scratch/report.json --implementation-label post-scheduling-gil-profile --worker-concurrency 8 --inference-batch-size 8 --queue-flush-max-wait-seconds 0.002
method.sampling: External 100 Hz stack sampling restricted to the Python thread holding the GIL. MCTS samples contain a ThreadPoolExecutor worker and MCTSAgent.choose_move, which excludes main-thread post-run replay validation.
method.classification: Exclusive deepest-stack/source-line classification. Nested win and legal-move functions take precedence; automatic-link rules are state transitions; direct tuple sorting and GameState._from_canonical are allocation/copy; choose_move lines 371-373 are backup and lines 375-461 are metadata construction.
limitations: Sampling percentages are relative evidence, not exact function timers.
The --gil view ranks executable Python work and intentionally omits native CUDA time and time workers spend waiting for inference or the GIL.
The profiled wall time is diagnostic; retained unprofiled runs remain the throughput source of truth.

thread_and_gil.interpretation: All eight game workers contributed GIL-held MCTS samples, but CPython permits only one of them to execute Python bytecode at a time. Threads overlap inference/native work and waits; they do not parallelize these ranked MCTS/game-tree paths.
thread_and_gil.measurement_boundary: This establishes balanced participation and serialized GIL ownership; it does not estimate per-worker GIL wait duration.

conclusion.remaining_end_to_end_bottleneck: The workload is on an overlapped inference/serialized-CPU plateau: inference and CPU/MCTS account for 48.26% and 47.90% of sampled wall state, while 2.43% average GPU utilization rules out saturated device compute. CPU MCTS/game-tree work is therefore a co-dominant end-to-end limiter, not background noise.
conclusion.ranked_next_target: Target expansion/initialization first. It is 42.04% of GIL-held MCTS samples; together with transition and state-copy work reached from expansion it accounts for 66.70%. Preserve selection and backup, which together are only 0.37%.
